classification: bounded vector with mathematical proof text, not a general kernel proof
domain: M0: finite fixed K, nonnegative normalized fixed w, p in (1/2,1), c in [0,1), cumulative-floor counts, fair ties, conditional independent Bernoulli emissions
fixedState: Condition on latent A with S(A)=1/2. Set T_N=sum correct bits, mu_N=E[T_N|A], sigma_N^2=Var(T_N|A).
steps: The proved quotas imply |mu_N-N/2|<=K because every q_l is in (0,1).
Every q_l >= (1-c)p and 1-q_l >= (1-c)(1-p). Thus sigma_N^2 >= kappa*N with kappa=(1-c)^2*p*(1-p)>0; sigma_N^2<=N/4.
Centered Bernoulli summands are bounded by 1, so their summed third absolute moments are at most sigma_N^2. Dividing by sigma_N^3 gives at most 1/sqrt(kappa*N), tending to zero.
Apply the independent, non-identically distributed normal-approximation theorem in dimension one to these standardized summands. Its error on half-lines tends to zero.
The standardized quota shift (N/2-mu_N)/sigma_N tends to zero. Therefore P(T_N<=N/2|A) tends to 1/2.
The approximation has a continuous limiting CDF, so the atom P(T_N=N/2|A) tends to zero. Fair tie handling changes the non-strict tail by half of this vanishing atom.
Hence conditional error tends to 1/2. Sum finitely many latent states with their declared product Bernoulli weights, combining this argument with the kernel-proved off-diagonal theorem.
